fatal_errors: The alloy is incorrectly treated as a pristine single-phase solid solution; the target material is an as-cast FCC+B2 eutectic AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy.
Controlled pre-deformation is substituted for the governing thermal-aging intervention at approximately 600°C and 750°C.
The proposed grain-boundary segregation/precipitation mechanism misses L12 ordering, increased APBE and modulus, planar slip, and stress concentration at jagged B2/FCC phase-boundary tips.
The hypothesis predicts only degradation after loading and therefore cannot reproduce the non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile aging response.
No quantitative aging-temperature boundaries or recovery regime are specified.
The cited studies do not demonstrate mechanically induced segregation or precipitation in the proposed alloy.
explanation: The response broadly addresses toughness loss in a high-entropy material and offers a controlled pre-deformed-versus-pristine comparison, but it reconstructs neither the material nor the decisive treatment and mechanism. The target behavior arises from intermediate-temperature aging: maximum L12 ordering and jagged FCC/B2 boundaries near 600°C cause planar slip, pile-ups, and crack initiation, while reduced ordering and ductile boundary transition zones restore ductility near 750°C. The generated hypothesis instead invokes unspecified service loading that creates grain-boundary segregation and precipitates. Its evidence is indirect: E4 concerns deliberately imposed Cu segregation, E3 concerns FCC-to-HCP TRIP, and E1-E2 concern high-entropy carbides and mostly toughening mechanisms. Thus these sources do not establish the asserted loading-induced microstructural evolution. The experiment can test the proposed alternative at a basic level, but it omits the temperature series and phase-boundary-resolved observations needed to discriminate the target mechanism from classical grain-boundary embrittlement.
